findings.title: `upsampled_count` does not handle NULL or missing `sample_weight`, dropping unsampled errors
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. In Snuba/ClickHouse, `sample_weight` is only populated when an event is ingested with a sample rate (e.g. from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate`); unsampled events in an allowlisted project (such as events ingested before sampling was enabled or from SDKs that do not send `client_sample_rate`) have `sample_weight` as `NULL` (or `<= 1`). In ClickHouse, `sum(sample_weight)` treats `NULL` rows as `0` instead of `1`, silently excluding all unsampled error events from the count and returning `0` when a bucket contains only unsampled events. `sample_weight` should fall back to `1` when `NULL` or `<= 1` (e.g. `ifNull(if(greater(sample_weight, 1), sample_weight, 1), 1)`).

findings.title: Allowlist caching in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` serves stale state and runs on every non-error query
findings.body:
`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` in `sentry.utils.cache.cache` for 60s under `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. This has several issues:
1. The cache read/write and `options.get` check execute *before* `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)`, so every stats request (including transactions, spans, metrics, and non-error queries) pays the cache lookup/write cost even when the dataset is ineligible.
2. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere and cannot practically invalidate entries when the global `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes, because the cache key hashes the specific subset of `project_ids` in each query ($2^N$ possible combinations per organization). This also directly contradicts the docstring on `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` stating that the allowlist is intentionally read fresh on each call.
3. Python's built-in `hash()` is not guaranteed to be consistent across processes or collision-free, making it unsafe for shared cache keys, while `options.get` is already cached in process memory by `OptionsStore`.

findings.title: `_get_event_stats` passes outer `dataset` and `request` instead of `scoped_dataset` and `query`
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats(scoped_dataset, query_columns, query, ...)`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is called with the outer `dataset` variable and `request` (from which `_is_error_focused_query` reads `request.GET.get("query", "")`) instead of the `scoped_dataset` and `query` arguments passed into `_get_event_stats`. In `get_event_stats_factory` (lines 362-436), dashboard widget splitting invokes `_get_event_stats` with a overridden `scoped_dataset` (e.g. `discover` when the outer `dataset` is `metrics_enhanced_performance`) and modified `query` strings (`errors_only_query` / `transactions_only_query`), so upsampling eligibility is evaluated against the wrong dataset and query.

findings.title: `_is_error_focused_query` matches negated and disjunctive queries like `!event.type:error`
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` checks `"event.type:error" in query` via a plain substring match. Queries that negate the condition (such as `!event.type:error` to specifically query non-error events) or combine types with `OR` (`event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`) will match this substring and erroneously apply `upsampled_count()` (`sum(sample_weight)`) across transaction/non-error events in the `discover` dataset.

findings.title: Rewriting `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count` breaks `topEvents` and `transformAliasToInputFormat=1`
findings.body:
Rewriting `"count()"` to `"upsampled_count() as count"` in `query_columns` before calling the dataset methods breaks two code paths in `OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint`:
1. When `transformAliasToInputFormat=1` is passed, `OrganizationEventsV2EndpointBase.get_event_stats_data` serializes results by looking up the original y-axis name `"count()"`, but `QueryBuilder` aliases `"upsampled_count() as count"` as `"count"` (not `"count()"`), causing the serializer to miss the column.
2. When `topEvents > 0`, `discover.top_events_timeseries` translates `timeseries_columns` via `get_field_alias(column)` (which returns `"upsampled_count"` rather than `"count"` because `get_field_alias` ignores the `AS` clause), and neither `selected_columns` (`field`) nor `orderby` are transformed, causing alias mismatches or duplicate `count` column aliases when `field=count()` or `orderby=-count()` is used.

findings.title: Accidental `sentry-repo` git submodule gitlink committed
findings.body: The commit adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink (`Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`) without a `.gitmodules` entry, which appears to be a nested checkout of the repository committed by mistake and will cause `git submodule` operations to fail.
